name: Customer support ticket: one case through tiered support
summary: This process handles one customer support case at a company that sells products and subscriptions online, from the customer's contact through triage, tier 1 handling with a knowledge lookup, and escalation where needed to tier 2 specialists, the billing back office or engineering. Refunds and credits above an agent's limit need a supervisor's approval, and solved tickets wait a few days for the customer to confirm before closing. Most cases are solved by tier 1 in minutes of work, but escalated ones wait in several queues, are re-keyed into other teams' tools, and draw chases and reopens when the first answer was wrong.

baseline.org_archetype: A US company of about 1,000 employees selling products and subscriptions online, with an in-house support team of about 70 agents in two tiers, a small billing back office and an engineering escalation rotation, all on a help desk tool linked to CRM and billing.
baseline.notes: Phone, email, web form and chat contacts; social media and outsourced support are excluded.

trigger: A customer emails, submits a web form, starts a chat or calls about a question, problem, bill or refund.
end_state: The ticket is closed after the customer confirms or does not reply, or is auto-solved after the customer stops responding.

volume.seasonality: Peaks after billing runs, product releases and holiday sales; quieter in summer.

evidence.note: About 50 tier 1 agents at roughly 500 handled tickets a month each (about 16 minutes of tier 1 work per ticket). Author estimate.

triggered_by.from: Billing and payments (failed payment or invoice notice)

systems.name: Help desk ticketing system with routing rules, macros and automations
Subscription billing and order management system
Knowledge base (internal and public help centre)

steps.name: Create ticket and route to queue
steps.description: An email, web form, chat or call creates a ticket in the help desk system, which sends an automatic acknowledgement, tags the channel and topic from the form fields, and routes it to the right tier 1 queue by language and product.
inputs: customer email, form, chat or call

error.defect_description: Wrong topic from the form, so the ticket lands in the wrong queue.

evidence.note: Ticketing and routing are standard help desk functions; misroute share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Identify and verify the customer
steps.description: When the ticket reaches the front of the queue, the agent opens it, finds the customer's account in the CRM and billing system by email or phone number, and asks verification questions before discussing or changing the account.

error.defect_description: Ticket linked to the wrong account or a duplicate customer record.

control.basis: Privacy and account security policy: verify identity before disclosing or changing account details (for regulated firms also sector privacy rules)

evidence.note: Email response averaged 12 hours 10 minutes in a 1,000-company test and 12 hours is the 'good' email benchmark, while calls and chats are answered in minutes; the mixed wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Triage and categorise
steps.description: The agent reads the request, sets the reason code and priority, merges duplicate tickets from the same customer and checks the status page for a known outage.

error.defect_description: Wrong reason code, which skews reporting and routing.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Search the knowledge base
steps.description: The agent searches internal articles and macros for the symptom or question, and opens the matching troubleshooting steps or policy page.

error.defect_description: Outdated article gives a wrong answer.

evidence.note: Search early and often is a KCS practice; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Troubleshoot and respond at tier 1
steps.description: The agent answers the question or walks through troubleshooting, makes simple account changes, and writes the reply from a macro, or decides the case needs a refund decision, tier 2, the back office or a supervisor.

error.defect_description: Wrong or incomplete answer, leading to a repeat contact.

next.condition: billing or payment problem for the back office

evidence.note: Industry FCR averages 71% (SQM) and tier 1 typically resolves 70% to 80%; 58% outright plus refunds within the agent's limit and returns after customer replies gives about 70%. Other shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for customer information
steps.description: The ticket is set to pending while the customer sends an order number, screenshot or test result; reminders go out automatically and silent tickets are solved after a few days.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Check refund or credit eligibility
steps.description: The agent opens the order or subscription in the billing system, checks dates, usage and earlier refunds against the refund policy, and works out the amount and whether it is within the agent's approval limit.

error.defect_description: Refund amount miscalculated or policy misapplied.

control.basis: Refund and credit policy: eligibility rules and agent approval limits

next.condition: eligible and within the agent limit
above the agent limit or an exception

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Issue refund or credit
steps.description: The agent enters the refund or account credit in the billing system or payment processor portal with a reason code, notes the transaction reference on the ticket, and tells the customer when the money will appear.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount or wrong order refunded, caught in reconciliation.

control.basis: FTC Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule: refunds for cancelled unshipped orders within seven working days or one billing cycle

evidence.note: Refund deadlines are stated by the FTC and apply only to cancelled or unshipped orders; refund handling by representatives is described by BLS.

steps.name: Escalate to tier 2
steps.description: The agent writes an internal note summarising the problem, what was tried and the customer's environment, tells the customer the case is with specialists, and reassigns the ticket to the tier 2 queue.

error.defect_description: Thin escalation note forces tier 2 to ask the customer again.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Tier 2 investigation
steps.description: A tier 2 specialist picks the ticket from the queue, reproduces the issue in the admin console or a test account, reads logs and decides whether to resolve it, involve engineering or the back office, or seek a refund approval.

next.condition: resolved with a new solution worth documenting

evidence.note: Tier 2 role described; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Log engineering bug report
steps.description: The specialist re-keys the problem into the engineering issue tracker with reproduction steps, account identifiers, logs and the number of customers affected, and links the support ticket to it.

error.defect_description: Missing reproduction steps delay engineering triage.

evidence.note: Tier 3 developers handle product issues; re-keying between tools is an author estimate.

steps.name: Engineering triage and response
steps.description: An engineer on the support rotation triages the bug in the next triage meeting, investigates, and provides a workaround, schedules a fix for a coming release, or declines it.

next.condition: will not fix, explain to customer

evidence.note: Developers as tier 3 described; queue times and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Supervisor approves refund or credit
steps.description: The supervisor reviews the request, the customer's value and history and the reason, and approves, reduces or declines the refund or goodwill credit in the help desk approval queue.
inputs: refund request with amount and reason

control.basis: Delegation of authority for refunds and credits: amounts above the agent limit need supervisor approval

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Submit back-office request
steps.description: The agent fills in the billing adjustment or payment investigation form, re-typing the account, invoice and transaction details, and tells the customer the billing team will follow up.

error.defect_description: Wrong invoice or transaction reference typed.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Back-office investigation and correction
steps.description: A billing specialist works the request queue once or twice a day, traces the payment or invoice in the billing system and processor portal, and corrects the invoice, retries the payment or issues a credit note.

error.defect_description: Adjustment posted to the wrong period or account.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: billing adjustments and credit notes reviewed and reconciled

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Reply to customer with the outcome
steps.description: The ticket owner writes to the customer with the fix, workaround, refund decision or explanation, and sets the ticket to solved.
inputs: resolution from tier 2, engineering, back office or supervisor

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022. Tier 1 keeps ownership of most tickets in this model.

steps.name: Supervisor handles complaint
steps.description: A supervisor calls or writes to an upset customer who asked for a manager or reopened an escalated case, reviews the history, apologises and decides on a remedy, sometimes a goodwill credit.

evidence.note: Referral to supervisors described by BLS; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for customer confirmation
steps.description: The ticket stays in solved status; the customer can reply to reopen it, and otherwise the help desk closes it automatically after a few days.

evidence.note: SQM: at a 71% FCR, 29% of customers contact again about the same issue; some repeat contacts arrive as new tickets, so the reopen share here is lower. Auto-close after about four days is an author estimate.

steps.name: Close ticket and send survey
steps.description: An automation closes the solved ticket and sends a one-question satisfaction survey; a small random sample is flagged for quality review.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Quality review of a sampled ticket
steps.description: A quality analyst scores the sampled ticket against the quality scorecard (verification, accuracy, tone, policy compliance) and sends feedback to the agent's supervisor.

control.basis: Support quality monitoring programme: scored sample of tickets per agent each month

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Write or update knowledge article
steps.description: The specialist writes a short article with the symptom, cause and steps, or fixes the existing one, so tier 1 can solve the next case without escalating.

evidence.note: Capture and improve practices of KCS; minutes are an author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for fix release
steps.description: The ticket is kept on hold, linked to the bug, until the fix ships in a scheduled release; the help desk then notifies the ticket owner.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Answer customer chase on an open ticket
steps.description: While the case waits on engineering, the customer writes or calls for an update; an agent reads the linked bug, replies with the status and adds a note.

evidence.note: Customers dislike repeating themselves and expect full context; the chase share is an author estimate.

exceptions.name: Escalation to tier 2
exceptions.description: Complex product or technical issues go to tier 2 specialists.

exceptions.name: Engineering involvement
exceptions.description: A product defect is logged for engineering; the customer waits for a workaround or a release.

exceptions.name: Refund or credit above agent limit
exceptions.description: A supervisor approves, reduces or declines the refund or goodwill credit.

exceptions.name: Back-office billing correction
exceptions.description: Billing or payment problems go to the billing team's request queue.

exceptions.name: Reopened ticket
exceptions.description: The customer replies that the problem is not fixed and the ticket goes back to triage.

exceptions.name: Customer stops responding
exceptions.description: A pending ticket is auto-solved after reminders go unanswered.

exceptions.name: Complaint to a supervisor
exceptions.description: The customer asks for a manager or reopens with a complaint.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from ticket creation to closed status (includes the solved-to-closed period)
benchmarks.population: Tiered support at mid-sized online sellers (composite estimate)

evidence.note: No opened source reports creation-to-closure times. Composite: first replies within about half a day for email (12 hours 10 minutes average in a test of 1,000 companies; 12 hours is the 'good' email benchmark), most tickets solved on that reply, then about three to four days before automatic closure; escalated tickets take days longer.

benchmarks.unit: share of contacts resolved without a repeat contact

benchmarks.population: SuperOffice test of 1,000 companies (2017 to 2018); Zendesk citing Toister

pain_points.description: Escalated cases are re-keyed into the engineering tracker or a back-office form and wait in each team's queue, while customers chase for updates.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

pain_points.description: Customers must repeat their problem when a ticket changes hands; 72% call this poor service.
Refunds above an agent's limit wait for a supervisor's approval.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice in tiered customer support teams using help desk software, 2019 to 2022.

pain_points.description: Wrong or incomplete first answers cause repeat contacts; about 29% of customers contact again at average first contact resolution.
Email queues build up so first replies take hours.

sources.title: First call resolution operating philosophy
sources.supports: Call centre industry benchmark first call resolution average 71%, world class 80% or higher; 29% of customers must contact again about the same issue; each 1% FCR gain lifts customer satisfaction 1%.

sources.title: Business guide to the FTC's Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule
sources.supports: Refunds for cancelled or unshipped orders within seven working days (cash, check or third-party credit) or one billing cycle (seller credit); refunds may not be replaced by store credit.

sources.title: KCS v6 practices guide
sources.supports: Knowledge-Centered Service solve loop: capture knowledge in the moment, structure, reuse (search early and often, linking), improve (reuse is review, flag it or fix it).

sources.title: Customer service benchmark report
sources.supports: Test of 1,000 companies: average response time to a customer service email 12 hours 10 minutes; 62% did not respond; only 20% answered fully on the first reply.

sources.title: 107 customer service statistics and facts you shouldn't ignore
sources.supports: Compiled statistics: 72% of customers say explaining a problem to multiple people is poor service; during the 2020 pandemic some companies saw escalations rise by more than 68% (HBR).

sources.title: First reply time: benchmarks and tips
sources.supports: First reply benchmarks: email good at 12 hours or less, better 4 hours, best 1 hour (Toister); social 5 hours; live chat 1 minute or less.

sources.title: Customer service statistics
sources.supports: 70% of customers expect anyone they interact with to have the full context; 3 in 10 agents cannot reliably access customer information.

sources.title: Customer service representatives (Occupational Outlook Handbook)
sources.supports: Representatives answer questions, handle complaints, orders, returns and billing, process refunds and exchanges, record contacts and refer customers to supervisors or more experienced staff; many work in call centres.

sources.title: Technical support (multi-tiered support)
sources.supports: Tier 1 gathers information and resolves straightforward problems, typically 70% to 80% of cases; tier 2 has deeper product knowledge; tier 3 is developers or back-end experts.

sources.title: May 2021 national occupational employment and wage estimates, United States
Employer costs for employee compensation, December 2021
sources.supports: Private industry wages and salaries were 70.5% of employer compensation costs; office and administrative support 69.7% (December 2021).

assumptions: Phone and chat contacts are answered in minutes and email or form tickets in hours; s02's wait mixes the channels.
Tier 1 keeps ownership of most tickets and sends the final reply (s16); some companies let tier 2 own escalated tickets.
Repeat contacts that arrive as new tickets are separate cases; only replies on the same ticket appear as reopens.
Solved tickets close automatically after about four days without a reply; this setting varies by company.
Refund settlement by the payment processor (several business days) happens after the ticket is solved and is not modelled as a step.
The FTC refund deadline applies only to cancelled or unshipped orders; other refunds follow company policy.
Loaded hourly cost = BLS May 2021 median wage x 1.42 benefits factor (ECEC December 2021) x 1.15 overhead factor.
The SQM benchmark page is current (2026) and does not date its figures; it is used as the best available FCR anchor.
